title: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 7 2024
description: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 7 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Marta said, "I am preparing for the examination." Which is the most appropriate reported form?
options: Marta said that she was preparing for the examination.
Marta said that I was preparing for the examination.
Marta told that she is preparing for the examination.
Marta said that she had prepared for the examination.
questions.explanation: Present continuous normally changes to past continuous, and I changes to she.

questions.questionText: The researcher said, "Water boils at 100°C." Which reported form is most appropriate when stating the scientific fact?
options: The researcher said that water had boiled at 100°C.
The researcher said that water boils at 100°C.
The researcher said that water was boiling at 100°C.
The researcher told that water boiled at 100°C.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts can remain in the original tense.

questions.questionText: Daniel said, "I have completed the assignment." Choose the correct reported speech.
options: Daniel said that he has completed the assignment.
Daniel said that he completed the assignment.
Daniel said that he had completed the assignment.
Daniel told that he had completed the assignment.
questions.explanation: Present perfect normally changes to past perfect.

questions.questionText: She said, "I saw the manager yesterday." Which sentence correctly reports her statement?
options: She said that she had seen the manager the day before.
She said that she saw the manager yesterday.
She told that she had seen the manager tomorrow.
She said that I had seen the manager the previous day.
questions.explanation: Past simple changes to past perfect and yesterday changes to the day before.

questions.questionText: Abel said, "I was studying when you called me." Choose the correct reported form.
options: Abel said that he was studying when I called him.
Abel said that he had been studying when I had called him.
Abel told that he had studied when I called him.
Abel said that he studied when I had called him.
questions.explanation: Past continuous normally changes to past perfect continuous in reported speech.

questions.questionText: Helen said to me, "I will help you tomorrow." Which is correct?
options: Helen said me that she would help me tomorrow.
Helen told me that she would help me the next day.
Helen told me that I would help her the next day.
Helen said that she will help me yesterday.
questions.explanation: Will becomes would, you becomes me, and tomorrow becomes the next day.

questions.questionText: The athlete said, "I can finish the race." Which reported form is correct?
options: The athlete said that he can finished the race.
The athlete told that he could finish the race.
The athlete said that he could finish the race.
The athlete said that he had finished the race.
questions.explanation: Can changes to could while the main verb remains in the base form.

questions.questionText: Ruth said, "I may visit them next week." Choose the correct reported sentence.
options: Ruth said that she might visit them the following week.
Ruth said that she may visited them next week.
Ruth told that she might visited them the previous week.
Ruth said that she would visit them last week.
questions.explanation: May changes to might and next week can change to the following week.

questions.questionText: The teacher said, "I have checked your papers." Which transformation is correct?
options: The teacher said that she had checked our papers.
The teacher told that she has checked our papers.
The teacher said that she checked your papers.
The teacher said that I had checked her papers.
questions.explanation: Present perfect changes to past perfect, with pronouns adjusted to context.

questions.questionText: Samuel said, "I had already left before noon." Which reported form is correct?
options: Samuel said that he has already left before noon.
Samuel said that he had already left before noon.
Samuel said that he had been leaving before noon.
Samuel told that he already left before noon.
questions.explanation: Past perfect normally remains unchanged in reported speech.

questions.questionText: Mimi said, "I live in Addis Ababa." If Mimi still lives there, which is acceptable?
options: Mimi said that she lived in Addis Ababa.
Mimi said that she lives in Addis Ababa.
Mimi told that she is living Addis Ababa.
Mimi said that she had lived in Addis Ababa.
questions.explanation: A continuing situation can remain in the present tense.

questions.questionText: The professor said, "The earth moves around the sun." Which reported form is most appropriate?
options: The professor said that the earth moved around the sun.
The professor said that the earth had moved around the sun.
The professor said that the earth moves around the sun.
The professor told that the earth was moving around the sun.
questions.explanation: A general scientific truth can remain in the present tense.

questions.questionText: John said to Mary, "I will send you the documents." Which sentence correctly reports this?
options: John told Mary that he would send her the documents.
John said Mary that he would send her the documents.
John told Mary that she would send him the documents.
John said that I would send Mary the documents.
questions.explanation: I becomes he and you becomes her.

questions.questionText: Sara said to me, "We saw them yesterday." Which is correct?
options: Sara told me that we had seen them the day before.
Sara told me that they had seen us yesterday.
Sara said me that we saw them the previous day.
Sara told me that we have seen them tomorrow.
questions.explanation: We remains we from Sara's perspective, past simple becomes past perfect, and yesterday becomes the day before.

questions.questionText: Peter said, "I am working here now." If the report is made from another place and later time, which is best?
options: Peter said that he was working there then.
Peter said that I was working here now.
Peter told that he had worked there tomorrow.
Peter said that he is working here yesterday.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous, here becomes there, and now becomes then.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'tell' correctly in reported speech?
options: He told that he was tired.
He told me that he was tired.
He told to me that he was tired.
He told that me he was tired.
questions.explanation: Tell normally requires an object such as me.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'say' correctly?
options: She said me that she was busy.
She said to me that she was busy.
She said me to be busy.
She said me she busy.
questions.explanation: Say does not normally take a person directly, but say to + person is possible.

questions.questionText: "Are you ready for the interview?" The manager asked me. Choose the correct report.
options: The manager asked me if was I ready for the interview.
The manager asked me whether I was ready for the interview.
The manager asked me whether was I ready for the interview.
The manager told me if I was ready for the interview.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions use if or whether and statement word order.

questions.questionText: She asked him, "Did you finish the project?" Which is correct?
options: She asked him did he finish the project.
She asked him if he had finished the project.
She asked him whether had he finished the project.
She told him if he had finished the project.
questions.explanation: Did you finish changes to whether/if he had finished.

questions.questionText: "Do you understand the instructions?" the examiner asked. Which is correct?
options: The examiner asked whether I understood the instructions.
The examiner asked whether did I understand the instructions.
The examiner asked that I understood the instructions.
The examiner told whether I understood the instructions.
questions.explanation: Present simple question becomes past simple with statement word order.

questions.questionText: "Where do you keep the documents?" she asked me. Which is correct?
options: She asked me where did I keep the documents.
She asked me where I kept the documents.
She asked me where had I kept the documents.
She told me where I kept the documents.
questions.explanation: WH-questions retain the WH-word but use statement word order.

questions.questionText: "Why did the machine stop?" the engineer asked. Choose the correct report.
options: The engineer asked why did the machine stop.
The engineer asked why the machine had stopped.
The engineer asked why had the machine stopped.
The engineer told why the machine had stopped.
questions.explanation: Past simple changes to past perfect and inversion disappears.

questions.questionText: "What are you doing here?" he asked her. Which reported form is correct?
options: He asked her what was she doing there.
He asked her what she had been doing there.
He asked her what she was doing here.
He told her what she was doing there.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous, and here changes to there.

questions.questionText: "When will you submit the assignment?" the teacher asked me.
options: The teacher asked me when would I submit the assignment.
The teacher asked me when I would submit the assignment.
The teacher asked me when I will submit the assignment.
The teacher told me when would I submit the assignment.
questions.explanation: Will becomes would and the reported clause uses statement order.

questions.questionText: "How can I solve this problem?" David asked the teacher. Which is correct?
options: David asked the teacher how could he solve that problem.
David asked the teacher how he could solve that problem.
David told the teacher how he could solve this problem.
David asked the teacher how can he solve that problem.
questions.explanation: Can becomes could, this becomes that, and question inversion disappears.

questions.questionText: The officer said to the driver, "Stop the car immediately." Which is the correct report?
options: The officer asked the driver that he stopped the car.
The officer told the driver to stop the car immediately.
The officer said the driver stop the car.
The officer told to the driver stopping the car.
questions.explanation: A command uses told + object + to + base verb.

questions.questionText: The doctor said to the patient, "Do not eat this food." Choose the correct reported form.
options: The doctor told the patient not to eat that food.
The doctor told the patient to not ate this food.
The doctor said the patient did not eat that food.
The doctor asked the patient not eating that food.
questions.explanation: A negative command uses object + not to + base verb.

questions.questionText: "Please wait outside," the receptionist said to me.
options: The receptionist told me that I waited outside.
The receptionist asked me to wait outside.
The receptionist asked whether I waited outside.
The receptionist suggested me waiting outside.
questions.explanation: A polite request uses asked + object + to + verb.

questions.questionText: "Please don't make any noise," the librarian said to the students.
options: The librarian asked the students not to make any noise.
The librarian asked the students to not made any noise.
The librarian told that the students did not make noise.
The librarian suggested the students not making noise.
questions.explanation: A negative request uses asked + object + not to + verb.

questions.questionText: The teacher said to me, "You should revise this chapter." Which is the best report?
options: The teacher advised me to revise that chapter.
The teacher advised that I revised this chapter.
The teacher told me that I should revised that chapter.
The teacher suggested me to revise that chapter.
questions.explanation: Advice can be reported with advised + object + to + verb.

questions.questionText: "Don't enter that room," the guard said to us.
options: The guard warned us not to enter that room.
The guard warned that we did not enter that room.
The guard told us don't enter that room.
The guard suggested us not entering that room.
questions.explanation: A warning against an action uses warned + object + not to + verb.

questions.questionText: "Let's leave before it gets dark," Hana said.
options: Hana suggested leaving before it got dark.
Hana suggested us to leave before it got dark.
Hana told that we left before it got dark.
Hana advised leaving us before it got dark.
questions.explanation: Let's suggestions can be reported with suggested + V-ing.

questions.questionText: "Let's study together tonight," the students said.
options: The students suggested to study together that night.
The students suggested studying together that night.
The students told studying together that night.
The students suggested us to study together tonight.
questions.explanation: Suggest can be followed by a gerund phrase.

questions.questionText: "Let's take a break," the manager said.
options: The manager suggested that we take a break.
The manager suggested us to take a break.
The manager told that we took a break.
The manager suggested that we took a break tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Suggest + that-clause can use the base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I will carry your suitcase," he said to her?
options: He offered to carry her suitcase.
He promised her carrying the suitcase.
He offered her that he carried the suitcase.
He asked her to carry his suitcase.
questions.explanation: An offer is commonly reported with offered to + verb.

questions.questionText: "I will never reveal your secret," she said to me.
options: She promised not to reveal my secret.
She suggested not revealing my secret.
She refused me to reveal my secret.
She promised me not revealing her secret.
questions.explanation: A promise can be expressed with promised not to + verb.

questions.questionText: "I won't answer the question," the witness said.
options: The witness refused to answer the question.
The witness promised answering the question.
The witness suggested to answer the question.
The witness advised not answering the question.
questions.explanation: Refusal is reported with refused to + verb.

questions.questionText: Which reported sentence correctly represents a question rather than a request?
options: He asked me to close the window.
He asked me if I had closed the window.
He told me to close the window.
He advised me to close the window.
questions.explanation: A question about whether an action occurred uses if/whether.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Could you help me with this problem?"
options: She asked me to help her with that problem.
She asked me if could I help her with that problem.
She told me that I helped her with that problem.
She suggested me to help her with that problem.
questions.explanation: The original question functions as a request, so ask + object + to-infinitive is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Which reporting verb is least appropriate for the sentence "Don't touch the equipment" when the speaker is warning someone about danger?
options: warned
told
ordered
suggested
questions.explanation: Suggested does not normally report a direct negative command in this structure.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "You must leave now," when the statement refers to a past obligation?
options: He said that I must leave now.
He said that I had to leave then.
He told that I had leave then.
He said that I have to leave now.
questions.explanation: Must referring to a past obligation can change to had to; now can become then.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "You must be careful" when the advice remains relevant?
options: He said that I had to be careful yesterday.
He said that I must be careful.
He told that I must careful.
He said that I had been careful.
questions.explanation: Must can remain unchanged when expressing continuing necessity or advice.

questions.questionText: The manager said, "We are considering a new policy." Which is correct?
options: The manager said that they were considering a new policy.
The manager said that we had considered a new policy.
The manager told that they are considering a new policy.
The manager said that they considered a new policy.
questions.explanation: Present continuous changes to past continuous.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I have been waiting here for two hours"?
options: He said that he had been waiting there for two hours.
He said that he has been waiting here for two hours.
He told that he was waiting there for two hours.
He said that I had been waiting there for two hours.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous normally changes to past perfect continuous.

questions.questionText: Which reported form is correct for "I will meet you here tomorrow"?
options: She said that she would meet me there the next day.
She said that she will meet me here tomorrow.
She told that I would meet her there the next day.
She said that she had met me there the day before.
questions.explanation: Will becomes would, you becomes me, here becomes there, and tomorrow becomes the next day.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "These are my books," she said?
options: She said that these were my books.
She said that those were her books.
She told that those are her books.
She said that those had been my books.
questions.explanation: These can become those and my becomes her.

questions.questionText: Which reported form correctly changes "I bought this computer last week"?
options: He said that he had bought that computer the previous week.
He said that he bought this computer last week.
He told that he had bought this computer next week.
He said that I had bought that computer the following week.
questions.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect, this becomes that, and last week becomes the previous week.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an incorrect use of a reporting verb?
options: She told me that she was busy.
He said that he was tired.
They asked whether we were ready.
She said me that she was leaving.
questions.explanation: Say cannot normally be followed directly by a person; use told me.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an incorrect reported-question structure?
options: He asked where I lived.
She asked whether I had finished.
They asked why had he left.
I asked what she wanted.
questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order: why he had left.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an incorrect reported-command structure?
options: He told me to sit down.
She ordered them to leave.
The officer instructed us to wait.
He told me don't touch it.
questions.explanation: Negative commands require told + object + not to + verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "She asked me, 'Have you finished the work?'"?
options: She asked me if I had finished the work.
She asked me if had I finished the work.
She asked me whether I have finish the work.
She told me whether I had finished the work.
questions.explanation: Present perfect changes to past perfect and question inversion disappears.

questions.questionText: "Has the train arrived?" he asked. Choose the correct reported form.
options: He asked whether the train had arrived.
He asked whether had the train arrived.
He asked that the train had arrived.
He told whether the train had arrived.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions use whether/if plus statement order.

questions.questionText: "Why are they waiting outside?" the director asked.
options: The director asked why were they waiting outside.
The director asked why they were waiting outside.
The director asked why they had waited outside.
The director told why they were waiting outside.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous without inversion.

questions.questionText: "Who broke the window?" the teacher asked.
options: The teacher asked who did break the window.
The teacher asked who had broken the window.
The teacher asked who did had broken the window.
The teacher told who had broken the window.
questions.explanation: The past action is reported in past perfect.

questions.questionText: "Where have you put my keys?" she asked him.
options: She asked him where had he put her keys.
She asked him where he had put her keys.
She asked him where he has put my keys.
She told him where he had put her keys.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect and my becomes her.

questions.questionText: "Will you attend the meeting tomorrow?" the director asked me.
options: The director asked me whether I would attend the meeting the next day.
The director asked me whether would I attend the meeting tomorrow.
The director told me whether I would attend the meeting the next day.
The director asked me if I will attended the meeting tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Will changes to would and tomorrow changes to the next day.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I can solve the problem myself," Lina said?
options: Lina said that she could solve the problem herself.
Lina said that she can solved the problem herself.
Lina told that I could solve the problem myself.
Lina said that she had solved the problem herself.
questions.explanation: Can changes to could; the statement does not say that she actually solved it.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I may not attend the conference," he said?
options: He said that he might not attend the conference.
He said that he may not attended the conference.
He told that he might not attended the conference.
He said that he would not attended the conference.
questions.explanation: May changes to might followed by the base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I was working when she arrived"?
options: He said that he had been working when she had arrived.
He said that he was working when she arrived.
He told that he had worked when she arrived.
He said that he had been working when she arrives.
questions.explanation: Past continuous normally backshifts to past perfect continuous.

questions.questionText: Which transformation best preserves the meaning of "He said, 'I am tired'"?
options: He said that he was tired.
He told that I was tired.
He asked whether he was tired.
He suggested that he be tired.
questions.explanation: The statement becomes a that-clause with appropriate pronoun and tense changes.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I saw her two days ago"?
options: He said that he had seen her two days before.
He said that he saw her two days ago.
He told that he had seen her two days later.
He said that I had seen her two days before.
questions.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect and ago changes to before.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "We will arrive next week"?
options: They said that they would arrive the following week.
They said that we would arrive the previous week.
They told that they will arrive next week.
They said that they had arrived the following week.
questions.explanation: Will becomes would and next week becomes the following week.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I am staying here today"?
options: She said that she was staying there that day.
She said that she is staying here today.
She told that I was staying there that day.
She said that she had stayed there the day before.
questions.explanation: Present continuous, here, and today normally shift in a changed reporting context.

questions.questionText: Which reported sentence is grammatically correct?
options: He asked me where was the station.
He asked me where the station was.
He asked me where did the station be.
He asked me where had the station been.
questions.explanation: Reported WH-questions use statement word order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Don't forget to bring your passport," she said to me?
options: She reminded me to bring my passport.
She reminded me that I brought her passport.
She suggested me to bring my passport.
She said me not forgetting my passport.
questions.explanation: Remind can be used with object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Please come to my birthday party," Anna said to John?
options: Anna invited John to come to her birthday party.
Anna asked whether John came to her birthday party.
Anna told John that he came to her birthday party.
Anna suggested John to come to her birthday party.
questions.explanation: An invitation can be reported with invited + object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I will do it," he said?
options: He promised to do it.
He promised doing it.
He suggested him to do it.
He refused to do it.
questions.explanation: A promise is reported with promised to + verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I won't participate," she said?
options: She refused to participate.
She promised to participate.
She offered participating.
She suggested to participate.
questions.explanation: Refuse + to-infinitive expresses refusal.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I will help you with the project," he said to me?
options: He offered to help me with the project.
He suggested helping me with the project.
He asked me to help him with the project.
He refused to help me with the project.
questions.explanation: The original statement expresses an offer.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "You should see a doctor," my friend said?
options: My friend advised me to see a doctor.
My friend suggested me to see a doctor.
My friend told that I saw a doctor.
My friend asked whether I saw a doctor.
questions.explanation: Advice is commonly reported with advised + object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "You must not enter this area," the guard said to us?
options: The guard warned us not to enter that area.
The guard warned that we did not enter this area.
The guard told us that we must not entering that area.
The guard suggested us not to enter that area.
questions.explanation: A warning against an action uses warned + object + not to + verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Work harder," the coach said to the players?
options: The coach told the players to work harder.
The coach said the players worked harder.
The coach asked whether the players worked harder.
The coach suggested the players to work harder.
questions.explanation: A command uses told + object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Don't open the file," the administrator said to me?
options: The administrator told me not to open the file.
The administrator told me don't open the file.
The administrator said me not opening the file.
The administrator asked me whether I opened the file.
questions.explanation: Negative commands use not to + base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Could you send me the report?"
options: He asked me to send him the report.
He asked me if could I send him the report.
He told me that I sent him the report.
He suggested me sending him the report.
questions.explanation: The polite question functions as a request.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Would you wait here?"
options: She asked me to wait there.
She asked me would I wait here.
She told me whether I waited there.
She suggested me to wait there.
questions.explanation: A polite request is reported using asked + object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Have you seen my notebook?"
options: He asked me if I had seen his notebook.
He asked me if had I seen his notebook.
He told me if I had seen my notebook.
He asked me whether I have saw his notebook.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect and my becomes his.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Why haven't you finished your work?"
options: The teacher asked why I hadn't finished my work.
The teacher asked why hadn't I finished my work.
The teacher told why I hadn't finished my work.
The teacher asked why I haven't finished my work.
questions.explanation: The present perfect negative changes to past perfect negative.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "What did you buy yesterday?"
options: She asked me what I had bought the day before.
She asked me what had I bought yesterday.
She told me what I bought the previous day.
She asked me what did I buy the day before.
questions.explanation: Past simple changes to past perfect and yesterday changes to the day before.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Where will they stay tonight?"
options: He asked where they would stay that night.
He asked where would they stay tonight.
He told where they would stay that night.
He asked where they will stay tonight.
questions.explanation: Will becomes would, tonight can become that night, and inversion disappears.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Can you explain this rule to me?"
options: She asked me if I could explain that rule to her.
She asked me if could I explain this rule to her.
She told me that I could explain this rule.
She asked me whether I can explained that rule.
questions.explanation: Can changes to could, this becomes that, and you/me references change according to context.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Are these your documents?"
options: He asked me whether those were my documents.
He asked me whether were those my documents.
He told me whether those had been my documents.
He asked me if these are your documents.
questions.explanation: This/these can shift to that/those and the question uses statement order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I am not feeling well," she said?
options: She said that she was not feeling well.
She told that she is not feeling well.
She said that I had not felt well.
She asked whether she was not feeling well.
questions.explanation: Present continuous changes to past continuous.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I don't understand the question," he said?
options: He said that he didn't understand the question.
He said that he doesn't understood the question.
He told that I didn't understand the question.
He asked that he didn't understand the question.
questions.explanation: Present simple negative changes to past simple negative.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I didn't recognize him," she said?
options: She said that she hadn't recognized him.
She said that she didn't recognized him.
She told that she hadn't recognize him.
She said that I hadn't recognized him.
questions.explanation: Past simple normally changes to past perfect.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I had never visited that place," he said?
options: He said that he had never visited that place.
He said that he had never visit that place.
He told that he has never visited that place.
He said that he would never visit that place.
questions.explanation: Past perfect normally remains unchanged.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I could swim when I was five," she said?
options: She said that she could swim when she was five.
She said that she had could swim when she was five.
She told that she could swam when she had five.
She said that she can swim when she was five.
questions.explanation: Could normally does not require further backshift.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I must finish this today," he said, when the obligation was specific to that past situation?
options: He said that he had to finish that that day.
He said that he had to finish it that day.
He told that he must finished it today.
He said that he has to finish it that day.
questions.explanation: Must referring to past obligation can become had to; today can become that day.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I live here," she said, when she still lives in the same place?
options: She said that she lived there.
She said that she lives here.
She told that she lived here.
She said that she had lived there.
questions.explanation: If the situation remains true, the present tense can remain.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "The earth is round," the teacher said?
options: The teacher said that the earth was round.
The teacher said that the earth is round.
The teacher told that the earth had been round.
The teacher asked whether the earth was round.
questions.explanation: A general truth can remain in the present tense.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "The sun rises in the east," the teacher said?
options: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
The teacher told that the sun had risen in the east.
The teacher asked whether the sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: General truths do not require backshift.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I am going to the library now," he said?
options: He said that he was going to the library then.
He said that he is going to the library now.
He told that I was going to the library then.
He said that he had gone to the library then.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous and now becomes then.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "We are leaving tomorrow," they said?
options: They said that they were leaving the next day.
They said that we were leaving tomorrow.
They told that they are leaving the following day.
They said that they had left the next day.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous and tomorrow becomes the next day.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I have never seen this before," he said?
options: He said that he had never seen that before.
He said that he has never seen this before.
He told that he had never saw that before.
He said that I had never seen that before.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect and this can become that.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "She was working here yesterday," he said?
options: He said that she had been working there the day before.
He said that she was working here yesterday.
He told that she had worked there tomorrow.
He said that she has been working there the previous day.
questions.explanation: Past continuous becomes past perfect continuous, here becomes there, and yesterday becomes the day before.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I will not attend the meeting," she said?
options: She said that she would not attend the meeting.
She said that she would not attended the meeting.
She told that she will not attend the meeting.
She said that she had not attended the meeting.
questions.explanation: Will changes to would followed by the base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I cannot solve this problem," he said?
options: He said that he could not solve that problem.
He said that he cannot solved this problem.
He told that he could not solved that problem.
He said that he had not solved that problem.
questions.explanation: Cannot changes to could not and this can become that.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "I may arrive late," she said?
options: She said that she might arrive late.
She said that she might arrived late.
She told that she may arrived late.
She said that she would arrived late.
questions.explanation: May changes to might followed by the base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Let's not waste any more time," the leader said?
options: The leader suggested not wasting any more time.
The leader suggested us not to waste any more time.
The leader told that we did not waste any more time.
The leader suggested to not wasted any more time.
questions.explanation: A negative suggestion can be reported with suggested + not + V-ing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Please remind me to call her," he said to me?
options: He asked me to remind him to call her.
He told me that I reminded him to call her.
He suggested me reminding him to call her.
He asked whether I called her.
questions.explanation: The original request becomes asked + object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reports "Don't forget that the meeting is tomorrow," she said to me?
options: She reminded me that the meeting was the next day.
She told me not forgetting the meeting tomorrow.
She suggested me to remember the meeting.
She asked me whether the meeting was tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Remind can introduce a that-clause, with the time expression shifted.
